newsitem.title: BELARUS: Thousands in Minsk protest over pro-Russia policy.
newsitem.headline: Thousands in Minsk protest over pro-Russia policy.

text.p: Up to five thousand demonstrators gathered in central Minsk on Sunday to protest against the pro-Russian policies of hardline President Alexander Lukashenko.

The gathering, initially scheduled to mark the 930th anniversary of Minsk's foundation, occurred one day after reports that Lukashenko and Russia's President Boris Yeltsin had agreed in principle to hold simultaneous national referendums on closer integration between their countries.
"We are older than Moscow," read one slogan. The Russian capital marks its 850th anniversary later this year.
The protesters waved Belarus' traditional red and white-striped flag, which Lukashenko has replaced with old Soviet symbols.
"This is the begining of the political spring in Belarus," Oles Byalyatski, a leader of the nationalist Belarussian People's Front, told the demonstrators.
"We will protest against Lukashenko. We won't allow our state to be converted into a Russian region," he said.

Russia's Interfax news agency on Saturday quoted sources close to Yeltsin as saying he would raise the issue of joint referendums in a speech to the Russian parliament next Thursday. It gave no further details.
Yeltsin first mooted the idea of holding referendums on closer integration between the two former Soviet republics in January in a letter to Lukashenko, who welcomed the suggestion.
But in recent weeks the Belarus leadership has made a series of statements making clear that Minsk regarded union with Russia as a convergence between two sovereign, independent and equal states.
Yeltsin and Lukashenko signed a pact last year on creating a "community" between the two Slav states but few moves have been made since then towards closer integration.
Lukashenko is expected to meet Yeltsin in Moscow next Friday and later the two national parliaments are due to hold a joint session to discuss the integration of the two countries.
The U.S. State Department slammed Belarus last Friday for failing to uphold democracy and human rights and announced it was halting all American aid to the country of 10 million.
